title: Batch coordinator heartbeat drift causing slot misallocation and tail latency regression
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Summary: During a Dedicated capacity scale-up event on 2025-02-17 we observed a recurring pattern of long-tail token latency and tenant-level unfairness. Root cause analysis shows the batch coordinator's heartbeat alignment drifted under high slot churn, causing repeated slot misallocation and transient batch starvation for lower-priority request groups. This ticket tracks remediation tasks, follow-ups, and telemetry improvements.

Scope: affects the continuous batching layer across dedicated pools running runtime-1.19 and earlier; observed in region us-west-2 during autoscaling bursts. Not a model regression but a scheduling/coordination failure that amplified under increased slot churn from scale-up.

Why this is unique: earlier incidents focused on coalescer timers and backpressure oscillation; this one is specifically due to heartbeat drift in the leader-based coordinator that allowed overlapping slot leases and delayed reclamation, leading to uneven batch formation and amplified tail latency for small requests.
timeline:
2025-02-17 22:05 UTC - Autoscaler increased pool by 40%
2025-02-17 22:10 UTC - First latency spike detected on per-tenant SLAs
2025-02-17 22:16 UTC - Routing fallback temporarily mitigated errors
2025-02-18 04:00 UTC - Initial hotfix: reduce heartbeat interval to force re-sync (mitigation only)
2025-02-19 to 2025-02-27 - Investigation, additional telemetry collection and VM replay load tests
2025-03-02 - Patch PR created to add leader election stabilization & deterministic reclaim (PR <= linked)
root_cause:
The batch coordinator uses a soft heartbeat to keep slot leases and leader state in sync across replicas. Under high churn the coordinator's local timers experienced drift relative to wall-clock (due to GC pauses and thread preemption), allowing two replicas to believe they owned overlapping slot ranges. This caused inconsistent slot assignment and delayed reclamation of empty slots, which prevented new small requests from being batched promptly. The result was intermittent batch starvation and a long tail in token latency for affected tenants.
Contributing factors: ephemeral VM CPU contention during scale-up, insufficient telemetry on slot-ownership transitions, and lack of a fast deterministic fallback when lease inconsistencies are detected.
impact_summary: Observed: 3x increase in 99th-token latency for small chat requests for ~18 minutes, affecting ~12 tenants during the event. No data loss, but several customers saw perceived service degradation and opened support tickets. No security impact. Estimated customer_impact: medium.
action_items: Implement leader-election stabilization: introduce a short randomized backoff and epoch counter to prevent overlapping leadership during rapid failover - owner: Brandon Liu - estimate: 3
Add deterministic slot reclamation path: when two conflicting owners are detected, run a synchronous reclaim for affected slot ranges to avoid delayed reclamation - owner: Aisha Khan - estimate: 5

Hardening: make coordinator timers resilient to thread preemption by switching to monotonic clock and detecting long scheduler pauses; add unit tests that simulate GC-like pauses - owner: Miguel Alvarez - estimate: 3
Improve telemetry: emit slot-ownership-change events, lease-expiry jitter histogram, and a heartbeat-drift metric to alert before latency surfaces - owner: Sofia Patel - estimate: 2
Create canary and load-test scenarios: add autoscale-burst job to replay the scale-up event in CI, validate no overlapping leadership occurs - owner: Performance Team - estimate: 4
Operational mitigation: add an emergency circuit-breaker that forces deterministic batching (strict time window) for 60s if slot-misallocation rate crosses threshold - owner: On-call - estimate: 1
Post-deploy runbook update: document detection thresholds, rollback criteria, and customer communication templates - owner: Brandon Liu - estimate: 1
comments: 2025-02-18 Sofia Patel: Initial investigation points to slot ownership races. I pushed a mitigation to reduce heartbeat interval which temporarily reduced the error rate. Filed telemetry collection task to capture expired lease counts.

2025-02-19 Miguel Alvarez: Replayed production trace in staging and reproduced slot overlap with GC simulation. Observed coordinator timers drift by ~120ms under pause scenarios. Preparing a patch to use CLOCK_MONOTONIC and added watchdog checks.
2025-02-22 Aisha Khan: Prototype for synchronous reclaim landed in my branch; needs review for contention impact. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1842
2025-02-25 Brandon Liu: Design review complete. Agreement to combine randomized backoff with epoch counters to avoid split-brain. Added load tests to CI and canary plan for runtime-1.21 rollout.

2025-03-01 Performance Team: Canary in us-west-2 successful for 2 hours under synthetic autoscale bursts with patched coordinator. No slot overlaps observed; telemetry shows heartbeat-drift metric within 10ms. Monitoring for 48h before full rollout.
2025-03-03 On-call rotation: Emergency circuit-breaker config added to runtime config map; default disabled. Will enable in the next incident if early-warning triggers fire.
